rejected.title: Finance for global business
card: Businesses that trade overseas need help from the financial sector. It offers four main services.
Changing currencies
Banks swap Australian dollars for foreign money, so a business can pay overseas sellers or be paid by overseas buyers.
Moving payments
Banks send money between countries, so a seller and a buyer far apart can complete a sale.
Insuring and lending
Insurers cover goods that are lost or damaged on the way. Banks lend money to pay for stock before it is sold.
rejected.remember: Finance helps trade by changing money, moving money, covering risk and lending.

a.q: Ella's shop in Perth buys tea from Sri Lanka and must pay in rupees. Which service does she need from a bank?
opts: Changing Australian dollars into rupees
Insuring the tea against damage at sea
Lending her money to open a second shop
Taking her deposit so the tea stays safe
a.why: Ella must pay in rupees, so she needs her dollars swapped for that currency. Insurance covers damage to goods, which is a different need from paying for them.
a.clue: The seller wants a different kind of money.

b.q: A Tasmanian farm ships cheese to Japan. A storm might ruin the cargo. Which service best protects the farm from that risk?
opts: Insurance for goods in transit
A loan to buy more stock
Changing yen into dollars
Sending payments overseas
b.why: Insurance pays out when goods are lost or damaged on the way, which is the storm risk. Changing currency or sending payments helps the sale get paid, but neither covers ruined cargo.
b.clue: Which service pays out if goods are damaged?
